title: Google is quietly making email verification less annoying in Chrome on Android
summary: Chrome can now verify supported email addresses without sending you to your inbox.
body: TL;DR Chrome 154 adds Email Verification support on Android, letting supported sites confirm your email address through the browser. The feature could replace the usual verification email or one-time code, but both the website and email provider must support Google’s protocol. Google says the Chrome feature is separate from Android’s Verified Email system for apps, though it is working to make the two experiences more consistent. Chrome already knows plenty about you when you’re filling out forms, from your saved addresses to payment details. But soon, it may also be able to quietly prove that an email address is really yours without sending you off to your inbox first. That idea has been taking shape on desktop for months, and with Chrome 154, it is finally making its way to Android. Google shares that it’s extending its Email Verification origin trial to Chrome for Android. The Verified Email section is appearing under Settings > Addresses and more , complete with an “Automatically confirm your emails” toggle.

title: ChatGPT users, your AI-written text will soon carry a hidden watermark
summary: The days of using ChatGPT to write your assignments and reports may be coming to an end.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR ChatGPT-generated text will soon carry an invisible watermark, starting in Europe. OpenAI’s detector can identify the watermark, but edits and shorter text can make detection harder. If you use ChatGPT to write, your AI-generated text could soon be identifiable as such. For years, AI tools have made it easy to generate everything from images and audio to human-like text. While AI-generated images, videos, and audio can often be identified using dedicated detection tools, AI-written text has largely escaped the same level of scrutiny. ChatGPT, in particular, has become one of the most widely used tools for generating text that can closely mimic human writing. Now, OpenAI says it plans to change that by introducing watermarks for text generated by ChatGPT and Codex.

title: Samsung may have found a smart way to speed up Galaxy S27 Ultra charging
summary: The trick could be sustaining higher charging speeds for longer.
body: TL;DR The Galaxy S27 Ultra is rumored to keep the same 60W charging rating as the S26 Ultra. But Samsung may make that 60W work harder, potentially cutting charging times despite a larger battery. It’s still unclear whether the improvements will remain exclusive to the S27 Ultra. Apple gave Samsung an unusual taste of its own numbers game this year. The iPhone 18 Pro Max arrived with a 5,391mAh rated battery, edging past the Galaxy S26 Ultra’s 5,000mAh cell, while Apple also substantially improved wired charging to match Samsung. While the next Galaxy Ultra is already rumored to respond with a 5,700mAh battery , Samsung may have another trick planned for getting that larger cell topped up faster. According to leaker WalleGalaxy , the Galaxy S27 Ultra will retain the S26 Ultra’s 60W charging rating. However, Samsung is reportedly working on charging optimizations that would let the phone hold higher power levels longer during the early stages of a charge.
